text:
zoe: quick check 1 - new "Service timeline" mock shows req/s + p95(ms) in one compact row. space is limited. do we: dual axis, stacked mini-rows, or single normalized axis with unit chips?
marco: avoid dual axis unless necessary. stacked mini-rows are clear but use more vertical space.
dina: single normalized axis + unit chips could work if we surface absolute units on hover and in an accessible summary. also worried about big latency spikes blowing the scale.
nash: propose "overflow badge": if values exceed visible range, show a small red badge at the top-right of the chart (e.g., "+3 spikes") that opens a popover with raw values. keeps canvas tidy.
zoe: love that. what about smoothing + capping interactions? if we cap visually, smoothing should be computed on raw values but render using capped points to avoid trend distortion.
marco: agree. and mark capped points with a subtle outline and include a dashed cap line with tooltip: "Values above 2500 ms capped for display."
dina: accessibility: add hidden text under chart: "Throughput (requests per second) and 95th percentile latency (milliseconds). Some extreme values are capped visually; open data popover for raw values." include full-unit words for SR.
nash: legend microcopy: visual chips "b7 req/s" and "b7 ms"; SR reads "Throughput, requests per second" etc. add a small "show raw" toggle in settings.
zoe: quick formatter example to add in Figma notes:
```
function formatTick(value, unit) {
  return unit === 'req/s' ? siShort(value) : Math.round(value) + ' ms'
}
```
marco: small UX nit: when user clicks overflow badge, popover should allow CSV export and a link "Open full chart" to expand canvas.
dina: action items: @marco add overflow badge & cap-line to mock, @zoe add SR hidden text and tooltip copy, @ash add CSV/export flow.
design-bot: summary created: "Prefer single axis with unit chips + overflow badge for clipped spikes; visual capping with capped-point markers and dashed cap line; smoothing computed on raw then rendered on capped values; provide popover with raw data and CSV export; include SR-friendly hidden summary."
zoe: thanks all, will iterate on the frame and tag you when done. :rocket:
